summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, Walpola Rahula studied at Vidyalankara Pirivena, the University of Calcutta, the University of Ceylon under G. P. Malalasekera, and the University of Paris/Sorbonne under Paul Demiéville. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (1964–1969) and held posts at Northwestern, Oxford, UCLA, and Swarthmore.

Walter Bruno Henning worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics after studying at the University of Göttingen (1926–1930). He held posts at the University of London and SOAS (1936–1961), Columbia University (1946–1947), and the University of California, Berkeley (1961–1967).

Walter Elliot worked in Indology, history/archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the East India Company College (~1819–1820) and the College of Fort St George (~1821–1823), and served as Private Secretary to Lord Elphinstone in the Government of Madras (1837–1842).

Walter Eugene Clark specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his A.B. and doctorate at Harvard University (~1899–1906) and studied under Richard Pischel (~1906–1907). He taught at the University of Chicago (1915–1927) and served as Wales Professor of Sanskrit at Harvard (1927–1950).

Walter Liebenthal specialized in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, studying at Berlin, Marburg, Heidelberg, Halle-Wittenberg, and Breslau under Max Walleser, Johannes Nobel, and Otto Strauß. He held posts at the Sino-Indian Institute, Peking University, Visva-Bharati, Sorbonne/University of Paris, and Tübingen.

Walter M. Spink was a scholar of history/archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College (~1945–1949) and Harvard University (~1949–1954, PhD), and held posts at Brandeis University (1956–1961) and the University of Michigan (~1961–2000).

Walter Nowick was a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied at the Juilliard School (~1946–1949) and under Zuigan Goto (1950–1965). He held a post at Kyoto Women's University and founded Moonspring Hermitage.

Walter Porzig specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Jena (~1913–1920) and under Wilhelm Streitberg (~1920–1923), and held posts at the universities of Leipzig (~1923–1925), Bern (~1925–1935), Jena (~1935–1945), and Mainz (~1951–1961).

Walter Ruben was an Indologist and philosopher. He held academic posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1927–1935), the University of Chile (~1949–1950), and the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1950–1965).

Walter Simon specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke and August Hermann Francke. He held posts at Humboldt University, Kiel, the National Library of China, and the University of London/SOAS (1936–1960).

Walter Slaje is an Indologist who completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Vienna (~1978–1993). He worked at Graz University Library (1984–1995) and served as Director at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2020).

Walter William Skeat was a linguist who was educated at King's College School, Highgate School, and Christ's College, University of Cambridge (~1854–1858). He held a post at the University of Cambridge from ~1878 to 1912.

Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Stanford University (~1902–1907) and the University of Oxford/Jesus College (1907), and was a disciple of Kazi Dawa Samdup (~1919–1922).

Walther Heissig specialized in Iranian/Central Asian and religious studies. He studied at the universities of Vienna, Berlin, Göttingen, and Bonn, and held posts at Peking University, Fu Jen Catholic University (~1941–1945), and the University of Bonn (1964).

Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich (~1900–1901) and the University of Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann (~1901–1904). He worked at the Prussian State Library (1907) and held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg (1920–1951).

Walther Wüst specialized in Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich (1920–1923), where he became an extraordinary professor (1932) and Dean of the Philosophical Faculty (1935–1945), and held posts with the Ahnenerbe (1936) and Deutsche Akademie (1943).

Wannaporn Rienjang is a scholar in history/archaeology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Cambridge. Her posts include positions at the British Museum, the University of Oxford (attested 2019–2022), and Thammasat University (attested 2022–2023).
Warren Crawford Cowgill worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and Yale University (~1952–1957, Ph.D.), where he became professor of linguistics in 1956.

Warren Lee Todd works in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Lancaster University under the doctoral supervision of Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, and also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Chogye Trichen Rinpoche, and Peter Harvey.

Warrin Ratanamalai works in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2007) supervised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, and also studied under Phra Sudhivorayan and Somjin Sammāpañño.
